title: Doc Palmer orchestra personnel
summary: First rehearsal with the full band and a rundown of its trumpets, trombone, saxes and rhythm section, praising Doc Palmer's ears and power.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: And finally, we had the rehearsal with the full band, Doc Palmer's band. And that was another thrill, to have a chance to rehearse with the whole ...(?)... At that time... I could give you the personnel, I think.

The leader was Doc Palmer on trumpet. We also had Zeke Bradley. And our lead trumpet was Man(?) Henderson. He only played the lead as long as it took Doc to learn it, because as soon as Doc learned it, he played the lead. Doc didn't read, but he had fantastic ears and fantastic power and fantastic sound on his trumpet. He is one of the great trumpet players. It's too bad that he wasn't recorded. He was really one of the greats during the Louis Armstrong era. A powerful trumpet player. And he could play all the lead solos, everything! So that was the trumpet section.
They had the one trombone, Butch Rose(?), the trombone player. Then we had Clarence Holliston playing the lead alto, I played the third alto part, and Lucious Stokes played the tenor.

And in the rhythm section, we had Paul Gayten playing the piano, and Luke Palmer played the sousaphone, and H.G. Hennington playing the tenor guitar and the banjo, and Mark Hannah(?) played the drums -- a very excellent drummer.
